title: Best Music Video Makers (2026): How to Hire One Online
description: How to hire a music video creator: filmed, animated or lyric videos, what the package should include, rights, price factors and red flags.
intro: A music video gives listeners something to watch on YouTube and short-form platforms, and it can bring new people to your song. Online creators make lyric videos, animated videos, visualizers and edits of footage you film yourself. Projects go wrong when the style is not agreed, footage or effects are not licensed, or the video is delivered in only one format. This guide helps you plan a video that fits your release.

faq.q: What types of music videos can I order online?
faq.a: Common types are lyric videos, animated videos, audio visualizers, and edits of footage you film. Some creators also offer AI-assisted visuals. Filmed productions with a crew are usually booked locally.

faq.q: Do I need to film anything?
faq.a: For an edit of performance or story footage, yes. For lyric videos, animations and visualizers, the creator usually works from your audio, cover art and ideas.
A horizontal video for YouTube, plus vertical clips for short-form platforms. Ask for both in the same order, with the song's best moments cut as teasers.

faq.q: Can the creator use stock footage?
faq.a: Yes, if it is licensed for commercial use and for music videos. Ask where footage and effects come from.
Confirm in writing that you may publish and monetize the video on all platforms you plan to use.
